title: Comparing fractions with the same bottom number
examples: How do I compare fractions with the same denominator?

explain.say: Two friends in Cairo share a long flatbread cut into 8 equal pieces. One eats 3 pieces and the other eats 5. Who ate more? Look at the bars: 3 eighths on top, 5 eighths below.

draw.text: Comparing fractions with the same bottom number

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: fractions of a pie. Can you see the whole pie and the one slice? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Comparing fractions with the same bottom number

explain.say: Both bars are cut into 8 equal pieces, so every piece is the same size. The bottom number, called the denominator, is the same: 8. So you just count the shaded eighths. Which bar has more?
5 eighths is longer than 3 eighths. When the bottom numbers match, the bigger top number wins. The top number is called the numerator, and it counts the shaded pieces. Easy, right?
Try fifths. 2 fifths on top, 4 fifths below. The pieces are the same size, so 4 fifths is bigger. Which is smaller: 7 tenths or 9 tenths?
Wonderful! Now look at 7 eighths and 8 eighths. 8 eighths fills the whole bar, so it equals 1 whole! Challenge: put 3 sixths, 1 sixth and 5 sixths in order, smallest first.

faq.a: 5 eighths is bigger. Both use eighths, which are the same size, and 5 pieces is more than 3 pieces.

faq.q: How do I compare fractions with the same denominator?
faq.a: When the bottom numbers are the same, the pieces are the same size. So just compare the top numbers: the bigger top number is the bigger fraction.
asks: How do I compare fractions with the same bottom number?

faq.a: The denominator is the bottom number of a fraction. It tells you how many equal parts the whole is cut into.
asks: What is the bottom number of a fraction?

faq.a: The numerator is the top number of a fraction. It tells you how many of the equal parts you have.
asks: What is the top number of a fraction?

faq.a: 8 eighths means all 8 of the 8 equal parts, so the whole bar is shaded. Any fraction with the same top and bottom number equals 1.

facts: A fraction with the same numerator and denominator, like 8/8, equals 1 whole.

quiz.why: All three are sevenths, so the one with the smallest top number, 2, is smallest.

wrong.2: 6/7 is the biggest of the three.

quiz.say: Compare 4 over 9 and 7 over 9. 4 over 9 is...
quiz.why: 4 ninths is less than 7 ninths, because 4 pieces are fewer than 7 pieces of the same size.

wrong.0: Greater than would mean 4 ninths is bigger, but it has fewer pieces.
wrong.2: They are not equal: 4 pieces and 7 pieces are different amounts.
